headline: Sculpture creates objects in real space—art you can walk around, touch, and experience from every angle
universal_truth: Different dimensions reveal different truths; perspective changes with position
fun_facts: Michelangelo said he didn't create David—he released him from the marble that imprisoned him
The Statue of Liberty was built in Paris, then shipped to New York in 350 pieces
Some sculptures are designed to be experienced by touch—art for hands, not just eyes
discussion_questions: How is experiencing a sculpture different from seeing a painting?
What can 3D art do that 2D art cannot?
What objects in your life are like sculptures—meant to be experienced from all angles?

hook.script: A painting shows one view. A sculpture occupies real space—you can circle it, see it from above, below, from every angle. Each position reveals something different. Sculpture is art that exists in the same world you do.

cliff.script: Sculptors work in a unique way—they must imagine their creation from every possible angle simultaneously. How do artists think in three dimensions?

options.text: They must consider every view at once—how the form looks from front, back, sides, above—and make it work from all perspectives
options.response: Yes. Sculptors hold multiple views in mind simultaneously. Unlike painters with one canvas, sculptors create an infinite number of potential views.

options.text: They create from one angle and adjust the others afterward
options.response: That might work for some, but great sculptors think holistically from the start...

fact1.title: Adding vs Subtracting
fact1.script: Sculptors work two ways: additive—building up with clay, welding metal—or subtractive—carving away stone or wood. Adding lets you fix mistakes. Subtracting is unforgiving—remove too much and it's gone. Different approaches, different thinking.

fact2.title: Material Matters
fact2.script: Each material has character. Marble is luminous but hard. Bronze is durable and detailed. Clay is forgiving and immediate. The material shapes what's possible. Sculptors collaborate with their materials, not just control them.

fact3.title: Public Space
fact3.script: Sculptures often live in public spaces—monuments, parks, plazas. They become landmarks, meeting points, symbols. Unlike paintings in galleries, sculptures live with people, weathering, aging, and becoming part of the environment.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Different dimensions reveal different truths. Sculpture teaches that perspective changes with position. Walking around a problem—seeing it from all angles—reveals what a single view cannot.

outro.script: That's Day 154. Tomorrow, we'll explore putting pictures on surfaces—printmaking. Until then, walk around something and notice how your view changes with each step.

growTrack.title: Multi-Angle Thinking - Walk Around Problems
growTrack.activity: Take a problem or decision you're facing and 'walk around it' like a sculpture. What does it look like from different angles? From other people's perspectives? The view from one position isn't the whole truth.
